about.title: About Me
about.p1: I’m Vladi Georgiev, a developer from Bulgaria based in Eindhoven. After studying electronic trades in high school I earned seven professional front-end certificates from Meta, and I haven’t stopped since: over the past year I’ve gone from simple front-ends to shipping full-stack, cross-platform apps.
about.p2: These days I work with React, Next.js and TypeScript on the web, Expo and React Native on mobile, and C# and Node with PostgreSQL and Microsoft SQL on the back end. I design everything in Figma, tinker with C++ for hardware, and in DevMatch I connected the app to external APIs and MCP-driven AI agents.

devmatch.title: DevMatch
devmatch.desc: A full-stack, AI-powered job assistant for developers. An Expo React Native app backed by a Node and Express API finds jobs, scores your resume against each listing with ATS analysis, and helps you apply with tailored cover letters.
devmatch.story1_title: One place to run the whole job hunt
devmatch.story1_body: Job hunting as a developer is scattered across a dozen tabs: finding roles, tailoring a resume for each one, writing cover letters, then tracking who you applied to. DevMatch pulls all of that into a single app that actually understands your resume.
devmatch.story2_title: Every job gets a match score
devmatch.story2_body: Listings are ranked with a calculated match percentage based on how your skills and resume line up with each role, so you spend your time on the jobs you are actually a fit for instead of scrolling endlessly.
devmatch.story3_body: Upload a PDF resume and the AI scores it against a specific job description the way an applicant tracking system would, then rewrites it to lift the match: a clear before and after jump, like 78 percent to 85 percent.
devmatch.story4_body: For any role, DevMatch auto-generates a tailored motivation letter you can set to a tone that fits: casual, professional, confident or creative, so applying is one tap instead of a blank page.
devmatch.story5_body: I built both sides: an Expo React Native app for Android, iOS and web, and a Node and Express backend with Prisma and PostgreSQL, secured with JWT auth. A dashboard ties it together with a saved to applied to interview funnel and recent activity.
devmatch.fact1: Full-stack and cross-platform: one Expo React Native codebase runs on Android, iOS and the web, talking to a Node and Express API with Prisma over PostgreSQL.
devmatch.fact2: Every listing shows a calculated match percentage, so the feed surfaces the roles that fit your resume first.
devmatch.fact3: The ATS boost scores your resume against a real job description and shows a measurable before and after lift, not just vague advice.
devmatch.fact4: Motivation letters are generated per job in four selectable tones (casual, professional, confident, creative).
devmatch.fact5: A saved, applied, interview and rejected funnel plus a recent-activity feed keep the whole application pipeline in one dashboard.
devmatch.outcome1: Cross-platform Expo app + typed Node/Prisma backend
devmatch.outcome2: AI ATS flow that scores and rewrites resumes per job
devmatch.outcome3: JWT auth, job matching, resume upload and tracking

ourgrid.title: OurGrid (Client OpenRemote)
ourgrid.desc: A platform demystifying 'grid congestion' for the company OpenRemote. I designed the UI and validated the UX with real users (students & coaches) to translate complex data into a clean React interface.
ourgrid.story1_title: Local grids are hitting their limit
ourgrid.story1_body: Heat pumps, EVs and solar panels are spreading far faster than the grid can be upgraded. When a whole neighbourhood draws power at the same peak hours, local transformers overload, raising the risk of outages, pushing up bills, and blocking new homes and EV chargers. Physically reinforcing the grid can take 3 to 5 years.
ourgrid.story2_title: Keep the grid in balance, together
ourgrid.story2_body: Instead of waiting years for hardware, OurGrid eases the peaks through the community. If neighbours shift a little flexible energy use away from the busiest hours, the same transformers can carry far more, with no digging required.
ourgrid.story3_body: The app links to your smart meter (P1 dongle), EV charger, battery and heat pump. It shows live power use and warns you when your area nears a peak. During a 'congestion challenge' it suggests simple actions, like delaying the EV charge or the laundry, and each one earns points and trophies for the energy you shift.
ourgrid.story4_title: A privacy-safe view of the whole neighbourhood
ourgrid.story4_body: Officials and grid managers get an aggregated dashboard: congestion hotspots on a live map, neighbourhood load curves, participation rates and total energy shifted. Everything is measured at transformer level, so no single household is ever exposed, with exportable GDPR-compliant reports.
ourgrid.story5_title: Turning dense grid data into a calm interface
ourgrid.story5_body: Built with OpenRemote in the Netherlands, I designed the split-view UI for residents and municipalities, validated the UX with real users, and translated technical IoT and grid-congestion data into clean, accessible React components.
ourgrid.fact1: The whole product splits into two experiences from a single landing screen: a gamified resident app and a municipal dashboard, so each audience only sees what's relevant to them.
ourgrid.fact2: 'Congestion challenges' turn demand-response into a game: stay under a live target during peak hours and collect points and trophies for the energy you move off-peak.
ourgrid.fact3: Every dashboard metric is aggregated at the transformer / neighbourhood level, so congestion maps and load curves reveal grid stress without ever exposing a single household (GDPR by design).
ourgrid.fact4: It runs alongside existing grid infrastructure (residents just connect a P1 dongle, EV charger, battery or heat pump), and the app never controls devices automatically; it only guides.
ourgrid.outcome1: Validated UX via testing with real users
ourgrid.outcome2: Architected a split-view UI for Residents vs. Municipalities
ourgrid.outcome3: Translated technical IoT data into accessible web components

visiobal.title: Visiobal (Client Visio)
visiobal.desc: An interactive audio ball that lets visually impaired people find, connect to and play with it through sound. A 3D-printed sphere houses an ESP32 that synthesises music on-device and pairs with a companion app over Bluetooth LE: scan to connect, set the volume, and switch between tracks.
visiobal.story1_body: Visio is an organisation that supports blind and visually impaired children. They wanted something these kids could simply play with, a toy that doesn't depend on sight. That brief became the VisioBall.
visiobal.story2_title: How do you play with a ball you can't see?
visiobal.story2_body: A ball is no fun to a blind child if they can't tell where it is. The VisioBall answers back with sound and light, so it can be located, reached for and interacted with, turning a plain sphere into inclusive play.
visiobal.story3_body: Inside a custom 3D-printed shell sits an ESP32 that synthesises its music live on-device (Mozzi + I2S), driving a speaker, an LED behaviour and sleep/wake power handling, all run from an onboard battery, with a volume dial on the outside.
visiobal.story4_body: The companion app (Expo + React Native) scans over Bluetooth LE with an animated radar, connects to the ball, then hands over control: a 3D model you can spin, a music player with volume and frequency, and simple commands like on/off, blink rate and sleep/wake. It ships in five languages with light and dark themes.
visiobal.story5_body: Across embedded and app: the ESP32 firmware that gives the ball its voice, and the React Native app that finds and controls it over Bluetooth. The whole point is inclusion, so a blind child can locate the ball by ear and just play.
visiobal.fact1: Runs on an ESP32 (PlatformIO + Arduino) and synthesises its music live on-device with the Mozzi audio library: triangle and square oscillators, ADSR envelopes and smoothing, played out over I2S.
visiobal.fact2: Ships with several built-in tracks: a bright C-major tune, a funky E-minor groove (with a cheeky blue note) and a slow G-major-pentatonic 'Zen' arc, all switchable from the app.
visiobal.fact3: Pairs with the companion app over Bluetooth LE: 'Scan for Ball' to connect, a live volume slider and play / skip controls, with sleep-wake power handling on the ball itself.
visiobal.fact4: Built for inclusive play; the whole point is that visually impaired users can locate and interact with the ball by sound.
visiobal.fact5: Custom 3D-printed enclosure packs the speaker, battery pack and a volume potentiometer around the ESP32 board.
visiobal.outcome1: Built and designed the companion app for the ball
visiobal.outcome2: Made the ball fully controllable from the app over Bluetooth LE
visiobal.outcome3: Accessible-by-design play for visually impaired users
